OUTRUN 2 ANDROID - SELECTABLE ASPECT RATIO (NATIVE 4:3 / WIDESCREEN 16:9 / ULTRAWIDE 21:9)
Implementation, patch, build and validation guide
=====================================================================================

0. SOURCE OF TRUTH AND WHAT WAS AND WAS NOT CHECKED
---------------------------------------------------
Source analysed: the uploaded archive Chihiro-XBERecomp-main.zip (the trEEgEcko/Chihiro fork sources), port
ports/OutRun2 only. An attempt to read https://github.com/trEEgEcko/Chihiro directly failed (fetch rate limit), so
nothing in this guide depends on the live repository page; the patch was generated and applied against the archive.

Checked by reading the repository code (every item below was read, none assumed):
  - matrix storage and how the renderer composes them (gpu/state.h, gpu/vulkan.cpp)
  - viewport structure and how the guest viewport reaches the host (gpu/state.h, gpu/vulkan.cpp)
  - the shader constant buffer shared by the C++ and the generated HLSL (gpu/shaders.h, gpu/shaders.cpp)
  - settings storage (app/app.h, app/settings.cpp, TOML via toml++)
  - the Android graphics menu (app/graphics_menu.cpp, ImGui)
  - presentation of the frame (gpu/vulkan_present.cpp)
  - the pause mechanism (core/host_pause.h)

NOT checkable here, and therefore NOT verified:
  - OutRun 2's own matrix state at run time. The game executable (the XBE) is not in the repository and the game was not
    run. Which draws the title makes with fixed function matrices, which with vertex programs, its vertical FOV and its
    frustum culling are unknown. The design below was therefore built so that it does not depend on that knowledge.
  - A full compile. The authoring environment has no Vulkan SDK, SDL3, toml++ or Android NDK. What WAS done: the patch
    applies cleanly to the pristine archive (git apply --check and patch -p1 --dry-run), the edited text was reviewed,
    the new Java was syntax-checked, and the geometry formulas were checked numerically. Build it (section 6) before
    trusting it.
  - Behaviour on the device. Section 8 is the test plan.

1. DESIGN (WHAT THE CODE DOES AND WHY)
--------------------------------------
1.1 Facts found in the code
  - The console always renders 4:3. The host render target is the guest surface size times ONE scalar:
    scale_ = app::RenderScale(guest_h) (settings.cpp, vulkan.cpp). The Output resolution setting only contributes its
    HEIGHT to that scalar. So the frame target is always 4:3 (640x480 times the scale).
  - The frame is put on screen by VulkanRenderer::BlitFrame (vulkan_present.cpp), which letterboxes the frame target into
    the swapchain image inside a viewport box. Before this patch the box was 16:9 if app::Widescreen() else 4:3.
    app::Widescreen() only derives from the Output resolution aspect; the guest is never told about it.
  - Matrices: State::transforms is std::array<std::array<float,16>,512>, indexed by D3DTRANSFORMSTATETYPE, row-major,
    row-vector convention (v * M). kTsView = 2, kTsProjection = 3, kTsWorld = 256 (vulkan.cpp). MatMul(x,y,o) computes
    o = x * y with o[r*4+c] = sum_k x[r*4+k] * y[k*4+c]. FillTransformConstants builds world*view*projection*vpm and
    uploads it transposed as DrawConstants::wvp (and wv, wvn, and the three blend sets) for the fixed function path.
    Programmable vertex programs get their constants in State::vsc (192 float4, hardware order = D3D register + 96).
  - Viewport: struct Viewport { uint32_t x, y, w, h; float min_z, max_z; } (state.h). The guest viewport is applied in the
    shader (vpm in FillTransformConstants; the epilogue maps window pixels to clip), the host viewport covers the whole
    target and the scissor clips to the guest viewport (SetViewportScissor).
  - Every vertex shader, fixed function and programmable alike, ends in the same epilogue (kVsEpilogue in shaders.cpp):
    window pixel position p -> q.x = p.x*2/surf.x - 1, q.y = 1 - p.y*2/surf.y, q.xyz *= p.w. Pre-transformed (screen
    space, XYZRHW) draws enter it as window pixels too.
  - Settings: app::Settings (app.h), read in app::Load() with toml++ (t["key"].value_or(default)), written by Table() in
    settings.cpp; the file name is kGame.settings = "settings.toml" (src/common/game_info.cpp), in app::ExeDir().
  - Android graphics menu: DrawGraphicsMenu in graphics_menu.cpp, ImGui, edits a copy "draft" and commits on
    "Apply and save" (ApplyDisplay(); Save()). Choice(label, value, values, names) is the combo helper.

1.2 The approach
  Let A = the chosen aspect (4/3, 16/9 or 21/9) and k = (4/3) / A  (1, 0.75, 0.5714).
  a) Vertex stage, every draw to the frame target: q.x *= k (one line in the epilogue, fed by a new DrawConstants member
     "wide"). For the fixed function path this is exactly the same as multiplying column 0 of the projection matrix by k
     (clip.x = sum_r v_r * P[r][0]); for vertex programs it is the same operation on the program's own output, which is
     the only way to reach a projection the renderer never sees as a matrix. It changes only x: vertical FOV, depth (z, w)
     and every y are untouched.
  b) Presentation: the (still 4:3) frame target is shown in a box of aspect A instead of 4:3/16:9. Squeezing x by k and
     showing the frame 1/k wider cancel exactly, so objects stay square. World geometry that used to lie outside the 4:3
     frustum edge now falls inside the wider picture: horizontal FOV grows, vertical FOV is unchanged.
  c) The 2D HUD and menus are drawn with pre-transformed vertices through the same epilogue, so they get the same squeeze
     and the same 1/k widening: their shapes stay natural, their layout is unchanged and sits centred in a 4:3 area. Their
     geometry is not otherwise touched.
  d) Native 4:3 (default): k = 1, box 4:3, so the output is the original image.

  Numeric check (illustration only, assumes a 45 degree vertical FOV because OutRun 2's real value is unknown):
     mode     k       horizontal FOV    shape of a unit object on screen (w/h)
     4:3      1.0000   57.82 deg         1.0000
     16:9     0.7500   72.73 deg         1.0000
     21:9     0.5714   88.05 deg         1.0000

1.3 Which draws are squeezed
  Only draws whose bound render target is a "frame target": the guest surface(s) passed to Present() (tracked in
  VulkanRenderer::frame_targets_, at most 8 addresses) plus any same-size target that the title copies INTO one of them
  (Copy()). Shadow maps, reflections and other offscreen targets are not squeezed. Before the first Present nothing is
  squeezed.

1.4 Deliberate departures from the literal wording of the request (read these)
  - "Do not stretch the framebuffer": the frame target is 4:3 because the runtime derives every host target size from a
    single scalar (scale_) and maps guest coordinates to targets uniformly (SetViewportScissor uses one scale for both
    axes, among others). A genuinely wider render target would need a non-uniform guest-to-target mapping through target
    creation, scissors, copies, read-backs and every screen pass. That cannot be done safely without running the game.
    Instead the picture is anamorphic: squeezed in the projection and un-squeezed on presentation. Shapes on screen are
    square (section 1.2), there is no crop and no zoom; but strictly speaking the presented image is a horizontally
    resampled 4:3 target.
  - "Separate world geometry and HUD/layout projection": the code has one vertex epilogue for everything and the renderer
    does not know which programmable draws are 2D. Both are squeezed by the same factor; as shown in 1.2 c) that is the
    correct treatment for each (extra world at the sides, natural-shaped centred HUD). Full-screen 2D quads (backgrounds,
    fades) therefore cover the central 4:3 area only.
  - "Expand the 3D projection's horizontal field of view through the projection matrices": done at the clip-space output
    of the vertex stage (equivalent to scaling the projection's x column, see 1.2 a) so that vertex programs are covered
    too. FillTransformConstants was not modified.
  - ports/OutRun2/config/game.toml was NOT modified: it is the static-recompilation configuration of the game, not the
    settings file. The setting is persisted in settings.toml as "aspect_ratio" (0 = native 4:3, 1 = 16:9, 2 = 21:9; any
    other stored value is reset to 0 on load).
  - gpu/d3d12.cpp was NOT modified: the Windows backend is out of scope for an Android-only build. It shares
    DrawConstants and the HLSL, never fills the new member (zero), and the shader treats zero as 1, so it is unchanged.
  - gpu/state.h was not modified: no new guest state is needed.

2. EXACT LIST OF MODIFIED FILES
-------------------------------
Native source and tests (all in outrun2_widescreen.patch, paths relative to the repository root):
  ports/OutRun2/sdk/runtime/app/app.h                 Settings::aspect; declarations of PresentAspect() and WideScale()
  ports/OutRun2/sdk/runtime/app/settings.cpp          load/save "aspect_ratio"; PresentAspect(); WideScale()
  ports/OutRun2/sdk/runtime/app/graphics_menu.cpp     "Aspect ratio" combo; committed on "Apply and save"
  ports/OutRun2/sdk/runtime/app/window_sdl.cpp        F9 cycles the three modes (the Android HUD aspect button sends F9)
  ports/OutRun2/sdk/runtime/gpu/shaders.h             DrawConstants::wide[4]
  ports/OutRun2/sdk/runtime/gpu/shaders.cpp           cbuffer member "float4 wide"; x squeeze in the vertex epilogue
  ports/OutRun2/sdk/runtime/gpu/vulkan.h              frame_targets_ (std::unordered_set<uint32_t>)
  ports/OutRun2/sdk/runtime/gpu/vulkan.cpp            wide constant in UploadConstants; frame target propagation in Copy()
  ports/OutRun2/sdk/runtime/gpu/vulkan_present.cpp    BlitFrame box from PresentAspect() with pre-rotation handling;
                                                      frame target registration in Present()
  ports/OutRun2/sdk/tests/test_shaders.cpp            layout test also checks the offset of "wide"
Named in the request but NOT modified: gpu/d3d12.cpp, gpu/state.h and config/game.toml (reasons in 1.4).
(gpu/vulkan.cpp IS modified, see the list above.)

Build and packaging files (outside the patch, delivered next to it):
  android-build.yml            the GitHub Actions workflow (steps added/removed, section 5)
  outrun2_patch.zip            Android resources and Java (HUD, icon, launcher/game activity)
  outrun2_widescreen.patch     the unified diff

Android pre-rotation note: BlitFrame now works the box out in screen terms and swaps its two fractions when the swapchain
is pre-rotated by 90 or 270 degrees. This fixes a defect seen on the target phone: with the original arithmetic the
4:3 and 16:9 boxes appeared as full-width bars at the top and bottom instead of bars at the sides (the compositor
transposes the buffer; measured heights of 864 and 648 pixels on a 2400x1080 screen matched the transposed boxes).

3. THE UNIFIED DIFF
-------------------
The complete diff is the file outrun2_widescreen.patch (226 lines, git format, paths a/ports/OutRun2/... b/ports/...).
It is delivered as a file because it is generated and checked against the archive; the guide does not retype it.

4. APPLYING THE PATCH
---------------------
Option A - through the GitHub workflow (no PC):
  1. In the fork, Add file > Upload files, and put outrun2_widescreen.patch in the folder .github/workflows/.
  2. Replace .github/workflows/android-build.yml with the delivered one. Its step "Apply OutRun2 widescreen patch" runs
     "git apply --check" and then "git apply" on that file before anything else touches the sources.
  3. Replace .github/workflows/outrun2_patch.zip with the delivered one.
Option B - on a PC, in a clone of the fork:
  cd Chihiro
  git apply --check outrun2_widescreen.patch
  git apply outrun2_widescreen.patch
  git add -A && git commit -m "OutRun 2: selectable aspect ratio"
Revert: git apply -R outrun2_widescreen.patch

If the older CI aspect steps are still in the workflow they detect the patch ("aspect_ratio" and "PresentAspect" already
present) and do nothing. Choosing Native 4:3 reproduces the original 4:3 image, i.e. what the unpatched build shows with a 4:3 box (the new shader
factor is 1.0). The unpatched build's own default on a wide Output resolution was an anamorphic 16:9 box; that default is gone.

5. WHAT THE DELIVERED WORKFLOW DOES (android-build.yml)
-------------------------------------------------------
Steps, in order (workflow_dispatch input "port"; use OutRun2):
  Host tools; Android SDK / NDK; Apply OutRun2 widescreen patch; Apply aspect ratio patch (no-op after the patch);
  Add F9 aspect hotkey (no-op after the patch); Fix touch aim for aspect modes (no-op for OutRun 2);
  Add pause hotkey (F8): F8 toggles a pure pause using host::Pause().Set() (the guest clocks and audio stop, the window
    keeps running, no settings panel); ignored while the graphics panel is open;
  Android defaults (OutRun2 only, take effect when no settings.toml exists yet): Fullscreen, 60 FPS limit, 2x texture
    filtering; aspect stays Native 4:3 as required;
  Apply HUD patch (unzips .github/workflows/outrun2_patch.zip); Fetch game archive (secret GAME_ARCHIVE_URL must be the
    Outrun 2.7z link); Generate native code; Build APK; upload artifact OutRun2-apk.
Removed from the workflow: the Test/Service wiring (it froze the game).
In outrun2_patch.zip: the HUD no longer has Test/Service buttons; the pause icon sends F8 (pure pause); the hamburger
opens Quick options with HUD opacity, Restart game, Exit to menu and Close (the graphics panel is no longer offered
there; R3/F10 on a gamepad or keyboard still opens it); Exit to menu returns to the launcher screen.

6. ANDROID BUILD COMMANDS
-------------------------
Requirements (android/README.md): Android SDK 35, build-tools 36.0.0, NDK 28.2.13676358, JDK 17, Python 3, cmake, ninja,
clang, p7zip. From ports/OutRun2 in the patched repository:
  python3 tools/prepare_game.py "/path/to/Outrun 2.7z"
  python3 tools/build_native.py --generate-only --jobs 3
  python3 tools/build_android.py --jobs 3
The APK is written under ports/OutRun2/android/build/. Optional flags of build_android.py: --deps-source, --deps-build,
--package-only. Source checks that need no game files: python3 tools/check_sources.py. Importer/launcher checks:
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v. Native GPU/input checks (including the extended layout test in
sdk/tests/test_shaders.cpp) run through: ctest --preset linux-release, after building their targets on a suitable Vulkan
host.
On GitHub: Actions > Android build > Run workflow > port OutRun2. The APK is the artifact "OutRun2-apk". A new signing key
is generated each run, so uninstall any previous build first.

7. USING IT
-----------
Graphics settings panel (opened with R3 on a gamepad or F10 on a keyboard; the touch HUD no longer opens it, so on a
phone without a gamepad the HUD aspect icon is the way to change the mode) > Aspect ratio: Native 4:3, Widescreen 16:9 (wider
view), Ultrawide 21:9 (wider view); "Apply and save" writes aspect_ratio to settings.toml. The HUD aspect icon sends F9
and cycles the three modes, saving each time. On a 20:9 phone 21:9 leaves thin bars at the top and bottom (21:9 is
narrower than 20:9 by height); 16:9 leaves bars at the sides.

8. VALIDATION PLAN
------------------
  1. Native 4:3: a 4:3 picture with bars at the sides (the unpatched 4:3 image). Nothing logged about widescreen.
  2. Choose 16:9 and race. Expected log line (once): "vulkan: widescreen x scale 0.7500 on frame target XXXXXXXX".
     21:9 logs 0.5714. If the line never appears the game does not render into a presented target (it draws offscreen and
     copies in a way this code does not see): report it, the picture would then be wrongly stretched.
  3. Shape test: wheels must be round, the speedometer circular, the car not widened. At the screen edges there must be
     scenery that native 4:3 cannot show (more road side, buildings).
  4. HUD: gauge, timers and score keep natural proportions and appear in a central 4:3 block.
  5. Menus (car select) appear as a centred 4:3 picture with natural shapes.
  6. Watch for: fades or transitions that cover only the centre; objects popping in at the side edges; reflections or
     post effects misplaced; doubled squeeze on any full-screen effect.
  7. Rotate the phone 180 degrees (sensorLandscape): the picture must stay correctly boxed.
  8. Pause icon: the game freezes without opening the settings panel; pressing it again resumes.
  9. Persistence: set 21:9, Exit to menu, Start game: the setting must remain.

9. KNOWN LIMITATIONS AND RISKS
------------------------------
  - Frustum culling is done by the game on the CPU against its own 4:3 frustum; objects just outside it are not submitted,
    so some pop-in at the new side edges is expected. Fixing it needs a change in the game code, not in the renderer.
  - Effects that sample the frame target (post processing) may be squeezed twice if the title renders a scene to one
    target and draws it to the frame through a pre-transformed quad. Not observable without running the game.
  - The frame target set is limited to 8 addresses and cleared if exceeded.
  - Full-screen 2D quads are confined to the central 4:3 area.
  - 21:9 on a 20:9 display is letterboxed by about 5 percent of the height.
  - d3d12 (Windows) does not implement the squeeze; Android builds use Vulkan only.
